sentenceSets.sentence: Her record on this particular question was unassailable, which is why the challenge focused on everything surrounding it.

answerChoices.reasoning: Impeccable (having no faults or errors) is very similar but emphasizes perfection rather than inability to be doubted or attacked.
Irrefutable (impossible to deny or disprove) is close but emphasizes logical impossibility rather than impermeability to attack.
Incontrovertible (not able to be disputed) is nearly identical but emphasizes logical impossibility more than impermeability.
Unquestionable (beyond doubt) overlaps but emphasizes certainty rather than impermeability to attack or question.
Flawless (having no defects) describes perfect quality but does not convey impermeability to attack.
Inviolable (must not be broken) emphasizes protection more than the specific inability to be attacked.
Airtight (so well constructed that nothing can get through) is metaphorical and emphasizes logical soundness rather than impermeability to doubt.
Questionable (open to doubt or suspicion) is the opposite of unassailable.
Vulnerable (capable of being wounded or attacked) is contrary to the impermeability of unassailable.
Disputable (open to debate or disagreement) opposes the undoubtable nature.
Weak (lacking strength or power) is opposite to impermeability to attack.

sentenceSets.sentence: The mathematician's proof was unassailable, built on axioms so fundamental that challenging it would require questioning the foundations of logic itself.

answerChoices.reasoning: Elegant (beautifully simple and effective) describes aesthetic quality but does not capture impermeability to attack or doubt.
Rigorous (extremely thorough and careful) describes methodology but does not convey impermeability to attack.
Sound (based on solid reasoning) overlaps but emphasizes correctness rather than impermeability to question.
Logical (based on reasoning) describes the nature but not specifically the quality of being beyond question.
Sophisticated (complex and refined) describes complexity but not impermeability to attack.
Comprehensive (complete and thorough) involves completeness but not the specific quality of being unassailable.
Conclusive (settling a question finally) describes finality but not impermeability to question.
Flawed (having defects) is opposite to the soundness of an unassailable proof.
Dubious (doubtful or uncertain) is the opposite of unassailable certainty.
Contestable (open to dispute) opposes the impermeability of unassailable.
Questionable (open to doubt) contradicts the impermeability to question.

sentenceSets.sentence: The defendant's alibi seemed unassailable until the prosecution introduced surveillance footage that contradicted the timeline.

answerChoices.reasoning: Airtight (leaving no room for doubt) is very similar but emphasizes logical closure rather than impermeability to attack.
Solid (firm and well-established) overlaps but emphasizes strength rather than impermeability to question.
Credible (capable of being believed) is close but describes trustworthiness rather than impermeability to attack.
Convincing (capable of persuading) overlaps but emphasizes persuasive power rather than impermeability.
Plausible (seeming reasonable) describes believability but not impermeability to question.
Consistent (in agreement with itself) describes internal agreement but not impermeability to external evidence.
Reliable (able to be trusted) describes dependability but not impermeability to attack.
Contradicted (proved wrong or in conflict) is the opposite of unassailable.
Questionable (open to doubt) opposes the impermeability of unassailable.
Vulnerable (capable of being wounded or attacked) is contrary to unassailable.
Dubious (doubtful or uncertain) contradicts the strength of unassailable.
